name: p17_det094
title: Biohub P17 DET094
purpose: DETECTION-SURFACE ARM. P9 (LB 0.925) with BIOHUB_DET_THRESHOLD 0.94 instead of the inherited 0.96875. Everything downstream is byte-identical, so this isolates the detection threshold exactly (Mendrika discussion/734604: keep the linker fixed while comparing detectors). Motivation, all VERIFIED: the metric charges over-prediction only 1 - 0.1 x over-prediction (Luka Duvanov discussion/733877), while edge recall ~ node recall^2 x conditional linking accuracy (Mendrika discussion/734604) -- so recall is quadratic and over-detection is nearly free. Alan Thanickal discussion/724917 measured that cutting nodes 17%% cost ~0.18 edge Jaccard, i.e. we sit on a steep part of the curve. Our own S1 detector sweep found F1 monotone DECREASING in threshold with the optimum at or below p0.50. NOTE: lowering a threshold on ONE detector does not create the near-duplicates that Duvanov warns cost ~9%% for nothing -- those come from unioning two models without a merge pass. The local-max NMS already dedupes within 1.625 um.
provenance: Single-variable arm off p9_coupled_division. CAUTION: detection-surface changes carry a measured ~3.5x LB amplification, and our only prior control (a 28%% node CUT) scored -0.032. Adding nodes is the untested direction; the metric line above bounds the downside at roughly -0.1 x over-prediction if edge Jaccard does not improve.
